title: Error Inspector side-panel: unified failed request & retry debugging UX
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a unified 'Error Inspector' side-panel in Redwood Console to make debugging failed inference requests and retries fast and safe. The panel surfaces an error taxonomy, retry timeline, raw payload inspection with redaction, and quick actions (re-run, escalate, link traces). Goal: reduce mean time to resolution for request-level failures and make root-cause triage accessible to engineers and SREs without leaving the Console.
acceptance_criteria: A list view of failed requests can be filtered by time range, route, model, status code, and error class
Clicking a failed request opens a right-side Error Inspector panel (not modal) that persists while navigating between list items

Inspector shows: summary, error taxonomy tag, retry timeline with timestamps and outcome, raw request/response (redacted), relevant headers, trace ID links, and top-level suggestion (retry/backoff/upgrade model)
Raw payload view allows toggling redaction on/off for users with permission; PII is redacted by default and redact rules are documented
Quick actions present: Re-run request (sandboxed), Create support ticket with prefilled context, Mark false positive, Add to investigation (creates linked incident in Ops dashboard)
Design passes accessibility review (keyboard focus, contrast, screen reader labels) and meets security review checklist for payload access
Prototype validated with a PM, 2 backend engineers, and an SRE in an internal design review session
decisions: Use a persistent right-side panel instead of a modal to allow quick comparison across multiple failed requests and to enable keyboard navigation between rows
Adopt a three-part inspector layout: Header (summary + taxonomy), Middle (timeline + bands for retries), Bottom (payload & actions). This maps well to existing Console patterns

Error taxonomy will be first-class tags: transient/network, auth/permission, rate-limit/quota, model-inference, payload/validation, infra (node OOM), unknown. Tags are surfaced with color-coding and suggested remediations
Raw payloads are shown in a collapsed JSON viewer with 'copy' and 'download' actions. Default view redacts fields matching PII patterns; explicit user toggle shown only to roles with permission
Quick actions will call well-defined backend routes and require confirmation for destructive ops (re-run on production will default to a sandboxed dry-run unless feature-flag enabled)
We will link trace IDs to the runtime trace viewer (existing internal tool) and include a deep-link for Dedicated/private deployments to query local logs

2025-07-20 - SRE (Danielle Park): requested inclusion of node_id and pod_id for infra errors and a quick link to the autoscaler dashboard
2025-07-22 - Security (Omar Liu): approved redaction-first UX, requested audit log entry for every payload view and that KMS policies be documented in PRD
2025-07-24 - Design critique (internal): moved from top-of-panel tabs to an accordion for payload sections to reduce visual weight; suggested inline microcopy for common remediation steps
notes: Prototype built in Figma with keyboard flows; interactive component shows timeline scrub and payload toggling
We considered a full-screen forensic view but rejected it to keep context with the failed requests list
Need engineering spike to determine cost of storing near-raw payloads for the retention window vs. storing references to S3 with time-limited access
Considerations for Private deployments: redaction rules must be configurable by on-prem admins and KMS integration must be plumbed through the private control plane
open_questions: What is the retention policy for raw request/response bodies for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? (legal & cost trade-offs)
Should re-run be rate-limited per account and require an audit event? What IAM level is required?
How do we surface aggregated error patterns derived from request samples without exposing PII? (sampling rules)
Is there appetite to allow customers to self-serve redaction rules in Console or should that remain internal?
implementation_notes: Backend needs new index for failed_requests with fields: route, model, error_tag, status_code, timestamp, retry_count, trace_id, storage_ref
Feature flag gate for 're-run production requests' and RBAC control for payload-unredact action
Add audit events: payload_viewed, request_rerun, false_positive_marked
Need to coordinate with Billing to expose linked billing events for requests in header
